thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - DNS resolution errors observed from azure-indiawest for Private deployments using ExpressRoute/On-prem egress. 37% failure rate to internal service hostnames. Auto-created INC-2106789. Please ack and state role.

sam: acked. I'm on-call. Paging network and infra. @raj @marta can you take a look?

raj: looking now. seeing NXDOMAIN and timeouts from Azure DNS forwarder VMs for the affected vnets. Initial suspicion: regional DNS resolver instability + intermittent path to on-prem DNS.

marta: I'm with CS, notifying impacted customers who have private peering + endpoints in ind-west. Preparing customer advisory draft.

ops-sre: I'm pulling control-plane logs and flow logs now. Noted elevated TCP retransmits between our NAT gateways and the ExpressRoute circuit.

sam: quick triage steps: 1) confirm whether this is Azure managed DNS or our forwarded on-prem resolver 2) check BGP state between gateway and customer edge 3) decide temporary fallback (static host overrides or route traffic to other region).

raj: digging BGP: `show bgp summary` on edge looks OK, sessions established. But I see route-flap counters incrementing on egress path to on-prem ASN intermittently. Could be transient flaps causing DNS responses to drop.

ops-sre: fetching packet captures from NAT VM:```
00:01:12.345 IP 10.2.3.4.53 > 10.5.6.7.42345: UDP, length 64
00:01:12.456 IP 10.2.3.4.53 > 10.5.6.7.42345: UDP, length 0 (truncated)
```
Looks like responses are not always completed.

kevin: can we flip DNS forwarding to use Azure's regional resolver as fallback for affected VNets while we stabilize the on-prem path? That would reduce NXDOMAINs for internal svc lookups (temporary risk: stale records).

raj: we can. But customers with strict on-prem DNS requirements might break. Need to check which customers require on-prem results.

marta: list of impacted customers from CS: AcmeApps (private), FinianCorp (private + regulatory), BetaLabs (staging only). FinianCorp is production-critical. Notifying them now.

natalie: I'll coordinate routing fallback. Plan: 1) enable Azure regional DNS fallback for 3 VNets (quick config change) 2) apply static /etc/hosts style overrides on our side for critical endpoints as emergency 3) if symptoms persist, shift traffic for affected workloads to europe-west2 (temporarily).

sam: do it in this order. Please post the exact commands and have rollback steps ready.

natalie: command to flip DNS forwarding (applies to vnet-svc-dns-rg):
```
az network dns resolver config update --resource-group vnet-svc-dns-rg --name ind-west-resolver --forwarders 168.63.129.16
```
Rollback = set the forwarders back to the on-prem resolver IPs.

ops-sre: applied DNS fallback to vnet-prod-1 and vnet-prod-2. Monitoring.

incident-bot: Note: change detected in cluster configs by @ops-sre at 2106789123.

marta: CS update sent to FinianCorp -> they are acknowledging, asked for ETA. They requested that we keep them in the loop for any route changes.

raj: I pushed a temporary BGP dampening tweak at the edge to reduce flap impact (config diff below):
```
! before
bgp dampening 0 0 0 0
! after
bgp dampening 30 2000 15 120
```
This should absorb short-lived withdraws. Monitoring BGP table now.

ops-sre: after enabling DNS fallback and dampening, DNS error rate dropped from 37% -> 9% over the last 6m. Latency spikes reduced.

kevin: good. For customers who need on-prem answers, we can push host overrides for the handful of critical hosts until full stabilization. I'll prepare the list.

marta: FinianCorp responded: "app owner saw reduced 502/timeout but still occasional token failures, please proceed with planned fallback if needed."

sam: decision checkpoint: continue monitoring 15m. If error rate <10% and FinianCorp confirms recovery, keep current config. If not, schedule regional traffic shift to europe-west2 for FinianCorp's production subnets.

natalie: 15m check-in: error rate steady at ~8%. FinianCorp reports degraded but functional. CS recommending hold and watch.

incident-bot: paging rotation: scheduled on-call handoff to @natalie in 20m.

raj: BGP flaps reduced, but I see a correlated increase in MPLS latency on the data path from provider side; raised ticket with transit provider (TP-51234). They acknowledged potential partial queue drop during peak.

ops-sre: adding a short-term mitigation: throttle retry storms from our side (reduce DNS client retries to minimize amplification). Patch applied to resolver pool: `dns-client --retries=2 --timeout=2s`

marta: updated customer advisory to say we're seeing partial DNS resolution issues caused by regional transit instability, mitigation in place, majority of customers restored, specific customers on watch.

kevin: deployed host overrides for critical tokens endpoints for FinianCorp and AcmeApps. Patches confirmed.

natalie: monitoring and metrics look stable for 45m. Error rates below 5%, latency normalized. Calling for wrap-up in 10m if no regressions.

sam: thanks all. Handoff: @natalie you'll take post-mitigation watch and follow up with provider for full RCA. @raj to follow BGP/ticket TP-51234. @marta to finalize customer timeline and post CS follow-up. @ops-sre to push config doc for dampening and retry limits.

customer-success: FinianCorp confirmed service recovered, requesting postmortem and timeline.

natalie: creating post-incident task list now. Quick notes for postmortem: timeline of initial detection (2106789012), mitigations (DNS fallback, BGP dampening, retry throttle, host overrides), affected customers, provider ticket ID TP-51234, follow-up actions (permanent route hardening, better failover for on-prem DNS, add synthetic monitors for private DNS paths).

sam: thanks. I'll mark this thread as incident-managed. Will close once PM/RCA ticket is created and CS has sent formal customer note.

natalie: RCA ticket created: RCA-2106789. Assigning to network eng. Closing watch window; will update any new findings here.

marta: CS update sent: advisory + customer-specific notes to FinianCorp, AcmeApps, BetaLabs.

natalie: concluding: incident mitigated, not fully resolved until provider confirms link stability. Keeping postmortem and action items open.

sam: closing the active incident channel, moving to postmortem in #postmortems. Thanks team :thumbsup:

natalie: :white_check_mark: closing notes posted to PM ticket."
